prime.options.path_tracing.tooltip: Switches between vanilla rasterization and Prime path tracing. The next frame boundary safely stops or recreates Prime's complete GPU pipeline, making this an in-game renderer restart; vanilla mode retains and runs no Prime path-tracing, denoising, or upscaling resources.
prime.options.experimental.voxel_texture: Within the 3×3×3 cluster window centered on the player's current 64-block cluster, replaces eligible unit block faces with instanced pixel-height meshes instead of rectangle-merged macro faces. LabPBR normal-map alpha supplies authored height when present; otherwise absolute base-texture luminance supplies the height. The darkest outer-border sample is aligned to the original block plane to soften seams. This can substantially increase BLAS and TLAS build cost.

Scales absolute luminance and authored LabPBR heights. At the default 100%, white or full authored height is 1/16 block; 0% is flat, and 200% gives 1/8 block before outer-border alignment. Changing it rebuilds the active 3×3×3 detail window.
prime.options.screenshot_mode.tooltip: Freezes the current camera, astronomy state, terrain, and animated block textures, then accumulates raw path estimates of Prime's current finite-bounce material model at native resolution. This completely bypasses DLSS RR, NRD, FSR, and all realtime debug overlays. Press Ctrl+Alt+F2 to enter or exit without affecting ordinary F2 screenshots; Escape only exits and never enters. This setting lasts only for the current game session.
prime.options.fsr.quality.tooltip: FSR (FidelityFX Super Resolution) path traces at a lower internal resolution and reconstructs the image at the window resolution. Higher quality preserves distant detail; higher performance usually improves frame rate. Choose a tier for the GPU, output resolution, scene, and target frame rate.
prime.options.post_processing.mode.toolt: Selects the complete realtime post-processing path. Supported RTX devices default to DLSS RR; unavailable or failed RR sessions fall back to NRD-FSR. Disabled presents native-resolution 1 spp noise directly and is intended only for inspecting the integrator. Reference screenshots are independent of this option.
prime.options.post_processing.quality.to: Controls the internal path-tracing resolution. NRD-FSR uses its established ratios; DLSS RR queries NVIDIA's exact dimensions for the selected tier; disabled post-processing always renders at native resolution. Performance is the default only to reduce the risk of a low-end device becoming unresponsive after restoring defaults; it is not a universal tier recommendation. Adjust it for the device, resolution, and scene.
prime.options.dlss_rr.debug_view.tooltip: Visualizes Prime's DLSS Ray Reconstruction inputs and reflection-motion construction guides. HDR colors use the common display transform while numeric guides use meaning-preserving mappings. It is available only while RR is active, does not reset history, and is never written to the config file.
prime.options.dlss_rr.debug_fullscreen.t: Shows the selected RR diagnostic across the screen instead of as a panel in the upper-right corner. This temporary state is never written to the config file.
prime.options.astronomy.latitude.tooltip: Sets the observer latitude used by the sun and celestial sphere. The full range is 90° south to 90° north; the default is 30° north. World east is +X, south is +Z, west is -X, and north is -Z.
prime.options.astronomy.season.tooltip: Sets the fixed annual position as apparent solar ecliptic longitude. It does not advance with Minecraft days. The four landmarks are the March equinox, June solstice, September equinox, and December solstice; seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere.
prime.options.lighting.sun_ev.tooltip: Exposure value (EV) changes direct sunlight, the sky, and atmospheric scattering together. Each step is 0.25 EV; adding 1 EV doubles brightness. Start with the default 0 EV and adjust it only when the whole outdoor scene looks too bright or too dark.
prime.options.lighting.star_ev.tooltip: Adjusts the embedded Gaia night sky independently. Each step is 0.25 EV; adding 1 EV doubles star brightness. Stars fade out during daylight and illuminate surfaces at night.
prime.options.lighting.block_light_ev.to: Exposure value (EV) changes illumination from emissive blocks such as torches and glowstone without changing which blocks emit light. Each step is 0.25 EV; adding 1 EV doubles brightness. Start with the default 0 EV.
prime.options.display.oklab_overexposure: Highlight overexposure controls how much brightness headroom the Oklab display transform gives to bright areas without changing the scene's physical lighting. The default 1.0× adds no overexposure. Higher values make the sun, lamps, and reflections brighter; excessive values can wash out detail.
prime.options.display.oklab_curve_expone: Controls how the display curve allocates dynamic range between shadows and highlights while keeping 18% middle gray fixed. The default is 0.75. Higher values make shadows more linear but compress highlight range and approach white sooner; lower values lift shadows and give highlights a gentler transition. This affects only the final display, not physical lighting or accumulation history.
prime.options.display.auto_exposure_comp: Controls how much of the metered exposure target is applied: 0% sets a neutral target, 100% follows the full metered target, and the default 50% balances adaptation in extreme scenes against stability. Higher values compensate scene brightness more fully but make exposure changes more pronounced. Final Exposure remains an independent adjustment.
Adds a final EV offset after automatic exposure. This is a pure display adjustment: it does not change physical lighting, reconstruction history, or screenshot accumulation, and can be adjusted live in screenshot mode.
prime.options.material.default_roughness: Roughness controls whether highlights are sharp or spread out and applies only to blocks without a PBR roughness texture. Lower values look smoother with tighter reflections; higher values look rougher with softer highlights. It never overrides roughness explicitly supplied by a resource pack. Keep the default 0.90 unless ordinary blocks look broadly too glossy or too matte.
prime.options.material.seamless_glass.to: Makes glass visually uniform by treating clear-glass border texels as the same smooth, colorless dielectric as its body and disabling frosted texels on stained glass. Volume color and absorption remain unchanged. Enabled by default; disable it to restore border and frosted regions authored in the material texture. Changing this resets temporal history.
prime.options.debug.triangle_distributio: Assigns each final ray-tracing triangle a stable random color and mixes it 50/50 with the original material color to inspect triangle distribution after merging and simplification. Lighting, transparency, and denoising continue normally. This setting lasts only for the current game session and does not affect reference screenshots.
prime.options.debug.renderer_diagnostics: Shows a read-only technical overlay with rendering mode and resolution, TLAS instance and triangle counts, light-tree size, automatic metering and exposure, and the full static-BLAS compaction lifecycle. Intended for troubleshooting and actionable bug reports; enabled only for the current game session.
prime.options.nrd.debug_view.tooltip: Presents actual NRD resources with nearest-neighbor scaling, bypassing FSR. Native validation preserves NRD colors and shows the current denoised result in its center; the three specular views use the shared Oklab display transform. Input/output SH0 show REBLUR's actual demodulated input and filtered output. Remodulated shows the signal after SH resolve, re-jitter and specular-albedo multiplication, immediately before final composition. Raw diagnostics: black is clean; magenta NaN; red/cyan positive/negative infinity; white mixed non-finite; blue finite negative; green rejected; pink invalid direction; violet above a unit range; yellow above the current FP16 limit of 65504. Switching does not reset history and is never written to the config file.
prime.options.fsr.debug_view.tooltip: Presents FidelityFX FSR's native integration overview while bypassing the Oklab display transform, preserving its labels, colors, and numeric range. Switching it does not reset history and it is never written to the config file.
